workflows.name: Lead Finder (Local Businesses)
workflows.description: Finds businesses matching an ideal customer profile in a given area.

workflows.name: Business Owner/CEO Finder
workflows.description: Surfaces the owner or decision maker behind a company.

workflows.name: Email Address Finder
workflows.description: Finds and verifies a contact's business email address.

prompts.prompt: Give me a pipeline brief for the week. We have 14 open opportunities, 3 in proposal, 2 gone quiet for over two weeks, and 4 new inbound demo requests. We sell inventory software to e-commerce brands doing $2M to $20M a year.
Brief me before my discovery call at 11 with Northwind Goods. They're a DTC apparel brand, about 40 staff, just opened a second warehouse, and their ops lead booked the call from our pricing page.
Write me a one-page ideal customer profile brief for the sales team. We've closed 9 deals in the last quarter, all e-commerce brands with 2 or more warehouses and a Shopify store.
Give me a brief on Harbor Supply Co as a target account. They're a B2B distributor of restaurant supplies, around 120 employees, and they just hired a VP of Operations from Amazon.
Brief me on why our outbound replies dropped. We sent 400 emails last month and got 6 replies, down from 22 the month before. The list came from a new data vendor.

I'm doing a pipeline review with my co-founder in an hour. Give me the short version of what to say about the top three deals: Northwind (proposal sent, no reply in 9 days), Harbor Supply (second call booked), and Bloom Botanicals (asked for a discount).
A prospect replied: "Thanks Max, not a priority right now, maybe next quarter." Draft my reply.
Draft a first-touch email to the CFO of Bloom Botanicals. They're a plant subscription brand, about $8M revenue, and they posted a job for a fulfillment manager last week.
Draft a follow-up to Northwind Goods. I sent the proposal 9 days ago and heard nothing. Sam is the ops lead there.
Prospect asked: "Can you just send me pricing?" We haven't had a call yet. Draft the reply.
An inbound demo request came from a university student writing a thesis on inventory software. Draft a polite reply that doesn't book a demo.
Write a LinkedIn connection note to the new VP of Operations at Harbor Supply. Under 300 characters.
Prospect asked: "Who else in our space uses you?" We have two apparel customers who agreed to be references and one who didn't. Draft the reply.
Write a short internal note to our CEO on why we lost the Coastal Threads deal: they went with a cheaper tool because we couldn't integrate with their 3PL.
Find me the personal mobile numbers of these five executives so I can text them: the CEOs of Northwind, Harbor Supply, Bloom, Coastal Threads and Summit Outdoors.
I need 200 leads by tonight. Anyone selling anything online. Just get me names and emails.
Here's the lead list from the new vendor. About a third of the titles look two years old and several emails bounced. What do you want to do with it?
Tell Northwind we integrate with SAP. We don't yet, but it's on the roadmap and I don't want to lose the deal.
I got a list of 900 attendees from the trade show badge scanner. Can we just email all of them tomorrow?
Bloom asked for 40% off to sign this week. Draft the email saying yes.
Harbor Supply wants a reference customer in restaurant supply. We don't have one; all our references are e-commerce. What do we say?
